verdict.rationale: LaunchDarkly documents a first-party Experimentation product that measures metrics such as page views, clicks and load time. It uses Bayesian statistics to highlight the leading variation and declare a winning one, and it can also run experiments on warehouse data. Community users confirm multivariate flags exist, so experiments can span more than two variations. Missing for 10: explicit docs on running multivariate (more than two arm) experiments, and independent or hands-on corroboration of the experimentation results workflow.

support.subject: As a product manager, I can run A/B and multivariate experiments on flags and see which variation wins on my metrics

citations.quote: You can measure things like page views, clicks, load time, infrastructure costs, and more.
LaunchDarkly highlights the leading variation when there is not yet enough experiment data to declare a winning variation.
You can also run experiments using data from an external warehouse, like Snowflake.
